problemText: Read this sentence from a story: 'The dog barked loudly when the mailman arrived at the gate.' Which part of this sentence is an EXPLICIT statement?
choices: The mailman felt scared by the dog's reaction because we must infer the mailman's emotions from context clues in the story.
The dog was protective of its owner's house based on what we can understand about the dog's behavior and purpose.
The dog barked loudly when the mailman arrived at the gate.
The dog had been trained to guard the property as shown by details we can figure out from the text.
hints: An explicit statement uses plain words that are written right there in the text.
Look for a fact you can point to word for word, with nothing to figure out.

problemText: Read this passage: 'Yuki had studied the spelling list every night for a week. On test day, she wrote each word carefully and checked her work twice before turning in her paper.' Which statement is an INFERENCE, not something the text states directly?
choices: Yuki studied the spelling list every night for a week.
The spelling test happened on a day Yuki had prepared for.
She checked her work twice before turning in her paper.
Yuki wanted to do well on the spelling test.
hints: An inference is something the text does not say in plain words but that you figure out from the details.
Look for a statement about what Yuki was thinking or feeling, not just what she did.

problemText:
A student read this passage and made the claim below. Is this claim an inference supported by textual evidence, or is it just restating something the text already says explicitly?

Passage: 'Kai arrived at soccer practice with his shin guards already on and his cleats laced tight.'

Student's claim: 'Kai arrived at soccer practice ready to play right away.'

Which is true?
choices: It is a valid inference because no sentence in the passage says Kai was ready to play.
It is just a restatement because the passage already says Kai had his shin guards on and cleats laced.
It is a guess because the passage does not explain why Kai wore his gear.
It is an assumption because being ready to play requires knowledge about soccer that the passage does not teach.
hints: Check whether any sentence in the passage uses the exact words 'ready to play.'
An inference combines details the text gives to reach a new conclusion; a restatement just rewrites what was already said.

problemText:
Read this passage, then decide which statement is a valid inference with proper textual evidence.

Passage: 'The library's new computer lab had been closed for three weeks. When it finally opened on Monday, there was a line of twenty students waiting at the door before the librarian unlocked it. By Wednesday, the computers were all taken up during lunch period, and a sign-up sheet had to be posted.'

Which inference below is best supported by evidence from the text?
choices: Students are not interested in using computers at school because they did not sign up for the scheduled time slots.
Students had been waiting to use the new computer lab and wanted to access it as soon as it became available.
The library ordered new computers because the old ones were broken and could no longer support student use.
The librarian decided to close the lab because too many students were using it at once and needed to manage access.
hints: Look for details showing student behavior and what those details suggest about student interest.
Point to the exact phrases that prove your answer: what did students do when the lab opened, and what does that tell you about how much they wanted it?

problemText:
A student read this passage and wrote an inference. Read both, then decide if the inference needs to be fixed because it includes information from outside the text.

Passage: 'Every afternoon at three o'clock, Mr. Chen locked his classroom door and walked to the gymnasium. He always carried a stack of clipboards and a whistle. The gymnasium was where students gathered for practice after school.'

Student's inference: 'Mr. Chen coaches a school sports team because he is athletic and loves to exercise.'

What should the student do to fix this inference?
choices: Change 'coaches' to 'works with' because the passage does not use the word coaches to describe Mr. Chen's role.
Remove the phrase 'a school sports team' because the passage never mentions a specific sport or team name.
Remove the phrase 'because he is athletic and loves to exercise' because those ideas come from outside the passage, not from its details.
Keep the entire inference but add supporting details about Mr. Chen's personality traits because the clipboard and whistle prove he must be someone who enjoys physical activity and fitness.
hints: An inference can only use details the passage itself provides; 'athletic' and 'loves to exercise' are not mentioned in the text.
Check whether the text actually says anything about why Mr. Chen does what he does, or whether the student added an outside belief.

problemText:
Read this passage, then answer the question that follows.

Passage: 'Jamila skipped her usual route through the park and took the long street instead. When she passed the old community center, she slowed down and stared at the colorful construction sign: NEW YOUTH CENTER OPENING NEXT MONTH. That evening, she spent two hours looking at the center's new website, clicked through every photo of the art studio, dance studio, and music room, and saved three pages of information in a folder.'

A reader makes this inference: 'Jamila is interested in the activities at the new youth center.' Which one of these is the BEST textual evidence to support that inference?
choices: Jamila took a long street instead of her usual route through the park, which shows she changed her normal behavior that day.
The construction sign said the center would open next month and displayed colorful information about the upcoming facility.
The youth center has an art studio, a dance studio, and a music room available for students to use.
She spent two hours looking at the website, clicked through every photo of the studios, and saved three pages of information.
hints: Look for the evidence that shows Jamila's own behavior and choices, not just facts about the building itself.
The strongest evidence shows what Jamila did with her time and attention, not just what exists at the center.

problemText: A story includes a sentence early on that says, 'The old bridge had a loose board near its middle that creaked loudly whenever anyone stepped on it.' Later, the main character runs across that bridge while being chased and the loose board gives way beneath them. What is the name of the job that the early sentence does in the story's overall structure?
choices: It is the rising action of the story.
It is a setup that the later moment depends on.
It is a summary of what happens at the bridge.
It is a location where the action takes place.
hints: Remember that a 'job' names what a part does for the rest of the story, not where it sits or what it says.
Think about whether the later chase scene would make sense without knowing about the loose board first.

problemText: Read this two-sentence passage: 'Kenji's art teacher assigned the class to paint something from nature, and Kenji chose the single dead oak tree that stood in his grandmother's yard. He spent three afternoons mixing shades of gray and brown until the tree looked exactly as bare and twisted as he remembered it.' How does the first sentence fit into the overall structure of these two sentences? Which of the following best describes its job?
choices: It provides factual information about where Kenji's teacher works and what subject she instructs.
It describes the assignment that the teacher gave and reveals which specific subject Kenji decided to paint for the class.
It sets up the dead oak tree as Kenji's subject, which the second sentence then shows him painting carefully.
It introduces Kenji as a character who attends art class and participates in classroom assignments.
hints: Look at what the second sentence does—what detail from the first sentence does it depend on?
A job in structure points to a later moment that needs it. The second sentence only makes sense if you already know Kenji chose which tree?

problemText: A story states: 'The community garden's tool shed had a broken padlock that hung open on the door.' Three sentences later, the story describes a teenager named Olivia taking a shovel from that shed without asking. How does the first sentence contribute to the overall structure of the story?
choices: It tells the reader about the physical appearance of the community garden and the condition of all its buildings and structures.
It provides information about why the community garden was created and what types of tools are usually stored in sheds.
It introduces a point in time before the story's main action where certain conditions exist in a specific location.
It establishes a detail about the setting—the broken padlock—that allows a later action to happen without a locked door stopping it.
hints: Think about what would have to change in the later sentence if the padlock were not broken.
A setting job establishes a place detail that matters again later. What detail about the shed becomes important when Olivia acts?

problemText: A student read a four-sentence story and was asked how a middle sentence fits the overall structure. The student answered: 'That sentence is where the conflict gets worse.' Explain what is wrong with that answer using the lesson vocabulary, then identify which of the following is a better answer.
choices: The student named a plot stage, not a job. A better answer would point to a specific later sentence and say what detail from the middle sentence that later sentence depends on.
The student identified a plot stage but neglected to trace how that stage creates a setup that a later sentence must pay off or resolve in order to show the sentence's actual function.
The student described the sentence's position in the story's sequence but failed to explain what detail or problem the sentence introduces that a later moment in the story then addresses or uses.
The student recognized what happens in the middle sentence but did not demonstrate how that content serves as a necessary setup for a payoff that appears afterward in the story.
hints: The lesson teaches the difference between a location (where a part sits) and a job (what it does). What did the student describe?
A job always requires you to point at the later moment that needs the part you are analyzing. Did the student do that?

problemText: Read this four-sentence story: 'Lena's violin had a loud squeak whenever she played a high note. Her orchestra teacher told her the instrument needed a professional repair. At the winter concert, Lena was supposed to play the opening solo. During her solo, a squeak rang out and the audience gasped.' Based on the lesson's definition of how a sentence fits the overall structure, which two sentences are connected by a setup-and-payoff relationship?
choices: Sentences 2 and 3: Sentence 2 establishes that the instrument requires professional care, and Sentence 3 puts Lena in a position where she must perform with that unrepaired instrument.
Sentences 1 and 4: Sentence 1 sets up the squeak problem, and Sentence 4 is where that problem causes the moment that matters in the story.
Sentences 1 and 2: Sentence 1 introduces a technical flaw in the violin, and Sentence 2 explains how a professional would address that flaw.
Sentences 3 and 4: Sentence 3 establishes that Lena will perform a solo piece, and Sentence 4 shows the audience's reaction to what happens during that solo.
hints: Remember that a payoff is the later moment where a setup actually matters to the story. Which sentence shows the consequence of the problem introduced earlier?
Ask yourself: if you removed one sentence, would the connection between setup and payoff still make sense? Test each pair.

problemText: A story includes these moments: (1) Early on, a character notices their neighbor has a vegetable garden but never invites anyone to visit it. (2) Much later, a character finds vegetable seeds in an old box and plants them secretly in the neighborhood's neglected shared garden. (3) At the very end, the neighbor discovers the new garden and begins tending it alongside the main character. The story is building toward a theme about people breaking down the walls between themselves. How do sentences 1 and 2 together fit into the overall structure, and why is sentence 3 the payoff for both?
choices: Sentence 1 presents a character's observation about gardening habits, Sentence 2 shows another character's independent gardening action, and Sentence 3 describes how two characters interact with plants together.
Sentences 1 and 2 each introduce a person involved with gardening in the neighborhood, and Sentence 3 resolves the gardening conflict by having both characters work in the same location.

Sentence 1 sets up the neighbor's isolation with their own garden, and Sentence 2 sets up the main character's action of planting seeds for sharing. Sentence 3 pays off both setups by showing them finally connecting through a shared garden instead of staying separate.

Sentence 1 identifies a location where gardening occurs and describes one person's approach to that activity, while Sentences 2 and 3 depict a series of gardening-related events that unfold in that same neighborhood setting.
hints: The lesson says a part can contribute to plot, setting, or theme. This story is building toward a theme—look at how the two early sentences each plant a piece of that theme idea.
Think about what readers learn from Sentence 1 (isolation) and what they learn from Sentence 2 (a gesture toward connection). How does Sentence 3 bring those two pieces together?

problemText: Read this passage about a character's response. 'When Jackson's ball rolled into the storm drain, he stared at the drain for a moment, then turned around and walked back to his house without saying anything.' Which of the following correctly describes what Jackson did in response to losing his ball?
choices: He stared at the drain, then walked back to his house without speaking.
He felt sad about losing his favorite toy and wanted to get another one from the store.
He was the kind of person who gave up easily and never faced problems directly.
He decided he would never play outside again because the drain was too dangerous.
hints: A response is what a character does, says, or thinks right after an event — look for actual actions or words in the text.
Do not pick an answer that claims a feeling or trait without showing what the character actually did.

problemText: Read the passage below. 'Chen had been avoiding his older sister all week after she borrowed his favorite comic book without asking. When she knocked on his bedroom door during dinner, Chen did not answer. After a few seconds, she left. That night, Chen quietly left the comic book on her desk before she got home from work.' What is the event that provokes Chen's response of leaving the comic book on her sister's desk?
choices: Chen's sister borrowed his favorite comic book without asking.
Chen's sister knocked on his bedroom door during dinner.
Chen avoided his older sister all week.
Chen's sister came home from work that night.
hints: The event that provokes a response comes right before the character acts. What happened immediately before Chen left the comic book on her desk?
A response must be connected to a specific moment in the story — the event that caused it.

problemText: A story says 'Aisha was brave when she entered the dark basement to find her lost cat.' Later, the text shows Aisha climbing slowly down the stairs, stopping to look around each corner before moving forward, and calling softly for the cat instead of yelling. Which statement best describes what the text actually shows versus what it claims?
choices: The text shows she is brave because it uses the word 'brave' to describe her.
The text proves she is brave by telling us she went into the dark basement.
The text claims she is brave but shows her moving carefully and calling softly.
The text claims she has a cat and shows her finding it in the basement.
hints: A claimed trait is a label the text uses in words; evidence is what the character actually does. The word 'brave' is a claim — what actions follow it?
Trust what you read about the character's actual steps and words over any single label the text assigns.

problemText: Read the two passages below that show the same character at different points in a story. At the beginning: 'Diego refused to try the new rock-climbing wall at the gym, saying he might fall and look foolish in front of the other members.' Later in the story: 'After his friend Rosa climbed the wall easily and cheered for Diego from the ground, Diego took off his shoes, gripped the first handhold, and climbed halfway up before sliding back down. When he reached the bottom, he grinned and said, "Again!" to Rosa.' Based on these two moments, which statement correctly describes how Diego changes?
choices: Diego changes because the rock-climbing wall becomes easier and safer after his first attempt at it.
Diego changes because Rosa climbs the wall successfully and Diego decides to be brave like her.
Diego changes from refusing to try climbing because he might fall to having made it halfway up the wall.
Diego changes from someone afraid to try climbing because he might fall to someone willing to attempt it despite the risk.
hints: A change compares the same kind of thing the character does at two different moments — not just describing one event as the change itself.
Look at what Diego says or does about climbing in the first moment and the last moment. What is different about his choice?

problemText: In a story, a character named Omar responds to a dropped glass by cleaning it up quickly, and the text states 'Omar was responsible.' Later, when Omar's homework assignment gets wet and ruins, he throws the ruined pages in the trash and does not redo the work before the deadline. Can you point to an event that proves Omar is responsible, based on what the text shows him doing across the whole story?
choices: No, because a claimed trait needs to be shown by the character's actions throughout the story, and his response to the ruined homework contradicts the label 'responsible.'
Yes, because Omar cleans up the dropped glass without being asked, which proves he has the character trait of responsibility in his daily life and habits.
Yes, because although Omar does not redo his homework, he still demonstrates responsibility by cleaning up the broken glass, and one good action counts as character evidence.
No, because Omar's failure to redo the homework assignment is a much larger problem than cleaning up a glass, so the small action does not prove he is truly responsible.
hints: A claimed trait is only evidence if the character's actions throughout the story match it. What does Omar actually do when faced with each problem?
Look at both moments: the dropped glass and the ruined homework. Do both actions show the same kind of behavior, or does one contradict the other?

problemText: Read the passage: 'In the first week of spring training, pitcher Marcus threw fast balls but refused to try throwing a curve ball, telling his coach, "Curve balls always go wild." During a game in mid-season, Marcus's fastball was not working, so his coach asked him to throw a curve ball. Marcus was sweating as he wound up for the pitch, but he threw it. The batter hit it into left field for an out. After the game, Marcus stayed late to practice curve balls with the coach, and by the final playoff game, Marcus threw three strikes using only curve balls and walked off the field saying "I can do both."' Based on the text, explain why "Marcus is talented" is a claimed trait and not evidence of how he changes, and identify what the text actually shows about his change.
choices: "Marcus is talented" is a claimed trait because it is a label for a character quality; his real change is that he learned to pitch during the season.
"Marcus is talented" is a claim because the text never uses that word; his real change is from refusing to throw curve balls to choosing to practice them and throwing them successfully in games.
"Marcus is talented" is a claimed trait because talent is not shown through actions; his real change is that he stopped throwing fastballs and only threw curve balls.
"Marcus is talented" is a claimed trait because the text does not say he is talented; his real change is that he got better at throwing and felt more confident about pitching.
hints: A claimed trait is a quality named in words without proof from actions. Compare what Marcus does at the start (refuses to try curve balls) to what he does at the end (practices and throws only curve balls successfully). That difference is the change.
The correct answer must name both the start moment and the end moment from the text, not just a general improvement or a single event.

problemText: Which of the following best describes what the exposition stage of a plot does?
choices: It builds tension through a series of complications that keep the outcome uncertain.
It shows the moment when the outcome of the story finally becomes decided.
It settles the conflict and shows what things look like after the turning point.
It introduces the characters, setting, and situation before any conflict appears.
hints: Exposition comes first, before any trouble starts.
Look for the stage that sets up the ordinary situation.

problemText:
Read the story below. Which sentence belongs in the rising action stage?

"For months, Elena practiced her presentation on the history of her neighborhood. On presentation day, the projector would not turn on, and the slides she had prepared disappeared from view. Elena took a deep breath and delivered the entire presentation from memory without the screen. The teacher gave her full credit and asked her to present again at the school assembly."

Which sentence is rising action?
choices: On presentation day, the projector would not turn on, and the slides she had prepared disappeared from view.
For months, Elena practiced her presentation on the history of her neighborhood, which is part of the exposition that sets up what Elena will do.
Elena took a deep breath and delivered the entire presentation from memory without the screen, which shows her solving the problem that was introduced.
The teacher gave her full credit and asked her to present again at the school assembly, which is the resolution that wraps up the story.
hints: Rising action introduces a complication that creates tension.
The outcome is not yet decided; something has gone wrong but Elena has not acted to fix it.

problemText:
Read the story below, then answer the question.

"Every weekend, Coach Torres ran a soccer clinic, and dozens of kids signed up because he always taught new tricks. This season, the clinic was cancelled three weeks in a row because of rain, and the kids grew frustrated with the empty field. When the fourth week arrived with clear skies, over a hundred kids showed up instead of the usual thirty, all eager to learn after the long wait. Coach Torres taught the best clinic of the year, and all the new kids asked to come back the next week."

Which pair correctly identifies both the climax and the resolution?
choices: Climax: 'Coach Torres taught the best clinic of the year.' Resolution: 'All the new kids asked to come back the next week.'

Climax: 'This season, the clinic was cancelled three weeks in a row because of rain, and the kids grew frustrated with the empty field.' Resolution: 'When the fourth week arrived with clear skies, over a hundred kids showed up instead of the usual thirty.'

Climax: 'When the fourth week arrived with clear skies, over a hundred kids showed up instead of the usual thirty.' Resolution: 'Coach Torres taught the best clinic of the year, and all the new kids asked to come back the next week.'
Climax: 'Over a hundred kids showed up instead of the usual thirty.' Resolution: 'Coach Torres taught the best clinic of the year, and all the new kids asked to come back the next week.'
hints: The climax is the turning point where the outcome becomes decided, not where the problem is most tense.
The resolution shows what happens after the turning point—the results of what became decided.

problemText:
Read the story below. A student labeled the plot stages but made one mistake in the order or assignment. Identify what is wrong.

"Jamal and his friend Kenji started a dog-walking business to earn money for a gaming system. On their first day, they arrived at a house where the owners did not answer the door, so they waited outside for twenty minutes. As they sat on the porch, one of the dogs got loose from the yard and ran down the street. Jamal chased the dog and caught it two blocks away, bringing it safely back to the owners who finally arrived home. The owners paid them extra and gave them five more dogs to walk every week."

Student's labels:
- Exposition: Jamal and his friend Kenji started a dog-walking business.
- Rising action: On their first day, they arrived at a house where the owners did not answer the door. / As they sat on the porch, one of the dogs got loose and ran down the street.
- Climax: Jamal chased the dog and caught it two blocks away.
- Resolution: The owners paid them extra and gave them five more dogs to walk.

Which plot stage was mislabeled?
choices: The exposition is too narrow; it should include the reason they started the business.
The rising action incorrectly includes the moment Jamal caught the dog, which is the turning point.
The resolution is mislabeled; it should begin after the owners arrive home and should include what happens next.
The climax should include 'bringing it safely back to the owners' because that is when the outcome becomes truly decided.
hints: The climax is one sentence where a decisive action turns the outcome—not just the beginning of that action.
Ask: at what exact moment does it become clear the problem is solved?

problemText:
Read the story below, then sort it into all four plot stages by identifying which sentences belong where.

"For three years, Amara had wanted to join the school debate team, but she was too nervous to try. The day before sign-ups closed, her best friend dared her to show up at the meeting. At the meeting, the team coach asked everyone to give a one-minute speech about any topic, and Amara's hands shook as she stood up. Amara spoke about why her neighborhood needed a community garden, and the coach clapped louder than anyone else. Amara signed up for the team that day and gave her first official speech at a tournament two weeks later."

Which answer correctly places all four stages in order?
choices: Exposition: For three years, Amara had wanted to join / Rising action: her friend dared her and the coach asked for speeches / Climax: Amara spoke about the community garden and the coach clapped / Resolution: she signed up and gave her first tournament speech
Exposition: wanting to join for three years / Rising action: the dare and the meeting / Climax: Amara stood up / Resolution: the coach clapped and she signed up

Exposition: For three years, Amara had wanted to join, but she was too nervous / Rising action: The day before sign-ups closed, her best friend dared her / Climax: Amara's hands shook as she stood up / Resolution: The coach clapped and Amara signed up

Exposition: Amara wanted to join the debate team / Rising action: she was nervous and her friend dared her / Climax: the coach asked for a one-minute speech / Resolution: Amara spoke and signed up for the team
hints: Remember: the climax is where something decisive HAPPENS—an action or choice that changes the outcome—not where the character feels most nervous or uncertain.
The resolution comes after the turning point and shows the results of what changed.
